prologue.title: Halloween, at last
prologue.narrator: Some nights, you think you're running toward a thrill. Sometimes, the thrill was waiting — still, patient.
prologue.text:
Your name is {{player}}, and you've been waiting for this moment for weeks.

Leo finally found a ladder to climb over the wall of Saint-Lunaire cemetery. Maya clutches her coat — and the bag of honey sweets she'd promised you for tonight. Sam is already filming everything on his phone. Inès packed three stories that are "actually scary."

The moon is full. Pumpkin lights still glow in the distance.

On the other side of the wall, the air changes: colder, heavier, as if the neighbourhood noise went out a second after everything else.

Leo whispers as he jumps: "One, two, three, four — we're all here?"

Four voices say yes. You say yes too. Nobody says your name.

You laugh anyway. You feel alive, excited, ready to scream at the slightest noise.

When you speak, the others carry on mid-sentence — as if you always arrive half a second too late.

choices.text: Be the first to dash toward the graves
Ask Inès to start with a story

legende.title: The tale of the fifth
legende.narrator: Yew trees don't grow here by chance. They keep the dead — and sometimes their habits.
legende.text:
Inès stops under a colonnade of trimmed yews. The branches brush the stones without a sound.

"Know the legend? Every Halloween, a ghost joins a group of teens in a cemetery. It thinks it's part of the crew. It laughs, screams, suggests dares…"

She speaks while looking down the alley, not really at your faces.

Maya shivers: "Great, thanks Inès."

"… and only at the end of the night does it understand that nobody could see it. They say it comes back every year. That it still thinks it's **its** night out."

Silence. Leo tries a laugh: "Well luckily there are four of us, not five! Come on Sam, film Maya's face."

Sam frames the group. You slip between Maya and Leo, sure you're in the centre.

When Sam lowers his phone, he doesn't look at you. He only says: "Perfect. Let's keep going."

choices.text: Challenge them: dare to enter the mausoleum
Notice Inès never said your name

defi.title: Truth or dare
defi.narrator: To dare is sometimes to walk where the living still hesitate — or where others won't follow you.
defi.text:
Leo pulls out an empty soda bottle — their summer "magic bottle," recycled for Halloween.

Truth or dare, cemetery edition. No backing out.

The bottle spins on a tilted slab. It slows… and stops in the empty space between you and Maya — touching no one.

"Well… that's {{player}}, right?" Maya says, laughing at the empty air.

Silence. Leo blinks, as if searching for someone he can't find: "Uh… fine. Dare anyway. Someone dare enter the Valmont mausoleum."

Nobody points at you. Yet you step forward.

An old lantern hangs on the rusted gate. You grab it. Your fingers don't feel it — but the flame lights, pale and straight.

In the glass, four faces reflect. Not five.

"Oh, stylish," Sam says. "Who lit that?"

You open your mouth. Nobody is waiting for you.

choices.text: Push the door and go in first
Count the reflections in the lantern

mausolee.title: The creaking door
mausolee.narrator: In the dark, you hear better what you refuse to see — especially when silence answers back.
mausolee.text:
The door creaks like an old laugh held back.

Inside smells of cold stone and dried wax. Names cover the walls: VALMONT, 1843–1921. Farther on, a newer stone — a Halloween date, a first name you don't read yet.

You try to breathe out to see your breath. Nothing shows.

Leo whistles: "OK, that's creepy. We leaving?"

You slip behind Maya to scare her — breath in, shout, hand on the shoulder…

Your hand passes through her coat like mist.

Maya still jumps and spins around, eyes wide.

"I felt… a chill," she says.

Leo stares at a point **behind** your shoulder, without seeing you: "Sam, you hear something?"

You laugh too loud. The mausoleum returns only your echo.

choices.text: Scream "BOO!" at the top of your lungs
Look at your hand through the flame

cabriole.title: Macabre hide-and-seek
cabriole.narrator: Sometimes you think you're writing the scare. Often you're only watching — or part of the set.
cabriole.text:
Outside, the game resumes. Hide-and-seek among the stones: whoever screams loudest wins.

You hide behind a marble angel. Its stone eyes seem to follow you — you alone.

Leo passes a metre away, looking for Maya.

"{{player}} must be on the other side," he says.

He doesn't look at you. He **walks through** where you're standing, without slowing.

You leap in front of him screaming.

Leo doesn't flinch. He frowns: "… Draft of cold air. Like last year."

*Like last year.* Nobody explains to you.

Sam raises his phone: "Selfie of the night! Come on, all four, squeeze in."

choices.text: Stand in the centre of the group
Count the shadows on the ground

photo.title: Four in the photo
photo.narrator: A picture doesn't lie. It only keeps what the living can hold.
photo.text:
Sam turns the screen.

Four faces: Leo sticking his tongue out, Maya wide-eyed, Inès dignified, Sam half cut off.

Where you stood — an orange blur, like breath on the lens. Like a hand that can't be caught.

"Ugly smudge," Leo says.

You whisper: "But I'm here…"

Inès doesn't look at the photo. She looks down a darker alley, toward the north of the cemetery.

"We're going that way," she says. "Like every year. Before we go home."

Maya clutches the bag of honey sweets. Sam pockets his phone without a word. Nobody laughs anymore.

brume.title: A voice in the fog
brume.narrator: When nobody answers, it isn't always because they aren't listening. Sometimes they're speaking to someone else.
brume.text:
Fog rises between the graves — thin, cold, clinging to the ground. It doesn't reach their ankles. It climbs to your chest.

You shout their names. Leo, Maya, Sam, Inès.

They walk ahead without slowing. You walk in their footsteps. Your feet leave no prints in the mud.

Inès speaks softly, toward the far alley: "{{player}}… if you can hear us…"

Maya clutches the bag of sweets: "Every year we say the same thing. Every year we come back. Even when we're scared to come back."

You don't understand yet.

You think they're praying for an absent friend — while **you** are right there, beside them.

Something tightens in your chest. A cold that has nothing to do with the fog.

tombe.title: Like every year
tombe.narrator: There comes a moment when the scare stops playing. It looks you in the eye — without blinking.
tombe.text:
They stop before a stone lighter than the others. Still almost new.

Then you read the name.

**{{player}}.** 2008–2025.

A Halloween date. A fall from the wall — the same ladder, maybe, you "came from" tonight. An ambulance that arrived too late.

The world tilts without a sound.

Maya sets the honey sweets at the foot of the stone — the ones she'd promised **for tonight**.

Leo lights a candle. His hand trembles slightly: "… As usual, {{player}}. We did the neighbourhood rounds without you. And we came back here. Always."

Sam murmurs: "We still had fun. Well — we tried."

Inès stares at the empty space beside the grave — exactly where you stand.

"We miss you," she says.

Not you. The person under the stone.

And suddenly you understand that **that person is you**.

choices.text: Read the date again — once, twice, three times

revelation.title: The fifth was you
revelation.narrator: The greatest twist isn't to scream. It's understanding why nobody ever screamed **with** you.
revelation.text:
Everything clicks — like a puzzle snapping shut, too late.

Inès's legend. The hand through the coat. The photo where you don't exist. The bottle stopping in empty air. Leo counting to four.

You didn't **re**join the crew tonight.

You **relived** the night you still thought you belonged — the night you fell, then every Halloween since, when your friends come to visit you… and you follow them, unknowing.

You're the ghost still playing truth or dare. Still hiding behind the stones. Still believing their laughter is **for** you.

They speak **about** you. Never **to** you.

Leo wipes a tear while trying to laugh: "OK. If {{player}} is here… knock over the candle. I'll save them a spot."

The flame wavers.

Nobody sees your hand. But the wax runs the wrong way.

choices.text: Blow out the candle — one last scare for them
Stay still — and let the flame burn

fin_rideau.title: Boo, guys
fin_rideau.narrator: Sometimes the best scream is the one you feel on your neck — without ever knowing who it's from.
fin_rideau.text:
You blow.

The candle goes out at once. As if someone closed a door across the whole cemetery.

Maya really screams this time. Leo steps back, pale. Sam nearly drops his phone. Inès doesn't move: "… There. You felt that?"

"OK OK OK," Leo pants. "That wasn't funny. Well it was. Well… **{{player}}**?"

Nobody sees you. Yet they **feel** something — a chill through their shoulders, a joke that lands at the wrong time.

They run for the exit yelling, happy and terrified — exactly how you'd have wanted it.

Behind them, among the yews, a light laugh. Maybe the wind. Maybe you.

You stay by the stone, smiling.

You're no longer the forgotten fifth. You're the ultimate Halloween joke.

**END — The perfect scare**

fin_veille.title: Watching without getting in the way
fin_veille.narrator: Some ghosts scream. Others just keep the candle lit — even when nobody knows why it still burns.
fin_veille.text:
You don't blow.

The candle stays upright. Small, stubborn, as if someone invisible shielded it from the wind.

Your friends leave at first light, eyes swollen. Maya turns once more: "See you next year, {{player}}. We'll come back. Get ready."

They don't know you hear them. They don't know you're already here every year, at their side — still believing the night is starting again.

Maybe one day you'll stop waiting. Maybe one day you'll simply watch over them.

Among the yews, the fog lifts. The cemetery falls silent again — but not empty. **Inhabited**.

**END — Guardian of the cemetery**
